newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Copper looking firm, eyes $2,400 again.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Copper looking firm, eyes $2,400 again.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Copper may charge higher towards the elusive $2,400 level after technical indicators resumed their uptrend in late trades Wednesday, chart experts said.
Aluminium also looked healthy after charts displayed a bullish "outside day" with prices ending above the previous day's high, but it needed to overcome $1,650 for fresh inroads.
COPPER - Wednesday's rebound from session lows to a strong finish of $2,385/90 touched a positive chord in copper, signalling another attempt to conquer the $2,400 barrier, analysts said.
Trading on Thursday was expected to be quiet owing to the public holiday in much of Europe.
News of a strike at Chile's Quebrada Blanca copper mine, coupled with stronger than expected U.S. first quarter GDP data, might have been the main reasons for late speculative short covering.
"The market remains fundamentally tight at present, and it will take a steady stream of copper flowing into the exchange to alter the bullish tone," said brokers GNI in a daily commentary.
LME stocks showed a small rise on Wednesday, but this trend would need to continue for some weeks to loosen the sentiment.

Analyst Martin Squires of brokers Rudolf Wolff said an "outside day" on copper charts, in which prices have a wider range than the previous day and end higher, suggested further challenges above $2,380 as the market re-targeted this year's high of $2,440.
"Also supportive of further strength is a bullish flag pattern that has been developing over the past week," he added.
Support came in strongly at the $2,320-$2,330 area.

After a last-minute attempt to avert a strike, workers at Quebrada Blanca rejected the company's final pay offer and began a strike action on Wednesday, paralysing the pit which has annual production of 75,000 tonnes of cathodes.
Quebrada Blanca is one Chile's smaller copper mines but the news was set to fuel fears of tight supply as workers at Chile's giant Escondida have been on strike for the last two weeks.
At 0730 GMT three month copper was indicated at $2,380/85 per tonne from Wednesday's close of $2,385/90.
ALUMINIUM - Stock drawdowns and a strong physical market were likely to keep aluminium underpinned, but the market needed to breach $1,650 to regain upside momentum, traders and analysts said.
If $1,650 could be overcome, aluminium would be able to reach towards $1,678-$1,680, they said. Support was pegged at around $1,620.
Brokers Brandeis said Wednesday's close was chart-friendly, but had not yet paved the way for substantial gains.

"A good close on the chart, although a better close would have been above $1,650. In addition, the appearance of a 'hanging man' on the candlestick chart indicates some indecision at the higher numbers," it said.
-- Clelia Oziel, London Newsroom +44-171-542 8071
